title: Fray

beats.what: Sophia is caught outside after her father's death; Kenny enforces the rule against going out
Boyd delivers a threat to Elgin dressed as community protection
Jim's body is discovered in the barn; Tabitha and the children confront it
Tabitha speaks a private farewell to Jim's body
Acosta steals the ambulance trying to drive out; Boyd deploys the tire strip
Ethan finds Boyd at the RV; Jim's ghost instructs him to find the Lake of Tears

character_beats.beat: Wants to grieve privately and protect her children, but Jade pressures her to act on their shared memories immediately; she expels him and insists the cost is too high
Wants to use Storywalking to undo her father's death; enters the ruins despite knowing she cannot change a told story
Wants community stability but the blackmail of Elgin is a second secret he is now carrying alongside the bullet stockpile

key_lines.line: This is the kind of thing that could tear this place apart.
key_lines.why: Boyd names fragmentation as the true threat, then acts to suppress truth rather than address it

key_lines.line: It should have been you hanging from the fucking rafter.
key_lines.why: Tabitha's grief erupts into the cruelest accusation of the season so far

key_lines.line: Lake of Tears? That's right. It's here, and I need you to find it.
key_lines.why: Jim's ghost plants the season's central quest object directly into Ethan

open_loops: What did Jim's ghost mean and why can he communicate through the Storywalk space?
Julie entered the ruins and glimpsed Jim but was pulled out; what did she actually see?
Sophia is now in the community without family; how does she integrate?
Acosta is contained but her drive-out impulse has not been resolved

contradiction.wants: To protect her children from false hope and the cost that comes with knowledge
contradiction.does: Refuses to tell people the truth about her and Jade's memories, then privately begins planning to reach the lighthouse alone

tone_notes: Episode runs at 63.6 words/min, the quietest dialogue rate across the seven episodes, matching its grief-and-dread register. Two long silences define the structure: 06:31-07:39 (68 sec) bridges Boyd's coercion of Elgin to the first discovery of Jim, and 49:14-50:16 (63 sec) precedes the RV scene with Ethan and Jim's ghost. Density spikes hard in minutes 11-12 (159 words/min) during the family's reaction to Jim's body.
